comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C62-C64 regarding MD simulation validation of ion conduction. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and supportive, with peer reviewers noting the simulations provide 'convincing evidence supporting the models.'

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C70-C72 regarding interaction network analysis and mutagenesis validation. Both evaluations find the structure-function relationship analysis well-supported, with peer reviewers praising the combination of methods.

Perfect agreement on claims C76-C79 regarding hERG-specific inactivation mechanisms. Both evaluations find the MD simulation evidence for sequential dilation convincing, with no concerns raised by peer reviewers.

Perfect agreement on claims C80-C83 regarding study limitations. Both evaluations view the transparent acknowledgment of limitations positively, with peer reviewers noting the authors appropriately acknowledged these issues.

Strong agreement on claims C57-C59, C73-C75 regarding structural comparisons and drug-binding mechanisms. Both find the structural analysis well-supported with clear figures and detailed insights, though OpenEval also includes C60-C61 which peer review addresses separately.

Significant disagreement on claims C47-C48, C51-C56 regarding conformation selection and validation. OpenEval finds the methodology and validation strongly supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about potential selection bias and whether pLDDT scores reliably indicate functional relevance despite authors' responses.

Agreement on claims C44-C46, C49-C50 regarding the overall AlphaFold2 methodology. Both evaluations find the approach well-described and using state-of-the-art methods, with peer reviewers accepting the template selection strategy explanation.

Disagreement on claims C67-C69 regarding correlation analysis and predictive improvement. OpenEval finds the quantitative correlation strongly supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about lack of appropriate controls and whether alternative AlphaFold conformations would yield similar improvements.

Partial agreement on claims C65-C66 regarding state-dependent drug binding. Both acknowledge qualitative agreement with experiments, but OpenEval notes rigid backbone limitations while peer reviewers raise broader concerns about controls and alternative structures.

Disagreement on claims C7-C8 regarding broader impact and generalizability. OpenEval finds the major findings well-supported as significant advances, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about generalizability and whether the method can be universally applied beyond systems with existing structural data.
OpenEval evaluated claims C1-C4, C15-C29 regarding biological and pharmacological context as well-supported background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C10-C12, C30-C31 regarding limitations of current methods and knowledge gaps as well-supported motivation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C13-C14, C32-C36 regarding AlphaFold2 capabilities and limitations as well-supported technical foundation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological background claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C18-C22, C37-C43 regarding established hERG structural and functional knowledge as well-supported background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C84-C90 regarding computational methods and Markov model as appropriately applied and innovative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
